topics.topic: Ownership and startup timing of the Linux-host prerequisite proof before mandatory O_NOFOLLOW use
questions: Which module owns proving the Linux-host prerequisite, and how may installation and store rely on it for unconditional O_NOFOLLOW use when both run before sandbox.probe_sandbox, the stated proof, and A20 rule 3 has no runtime owner?

Which module owns the Linux-host requirement and the decision that startup has proved it, given that State 3 says A20 rule 3 is outside the running kernel and has no module owner, while `sandbox` owns the A03 startup probe?

How can startup prove the Linux-host condition through A03 only after `installation` and `store` have already performed mandatory Linux-specific `O_NOFOLLOW` opens, with no availability check or non-Linux mode permitted?

Does `sandbox.probe_sandbox` own and perform the new runtime proof that the host is Linux and supports the pinned sandbox runtime, or is the Linux-only constraint entirely a release-build fact with no runtime host check?

quotes:
The owner decided on 2026-10-18: the kernel runs only on Linux, of any
    version that runs the sandbox runtime — the start already proves the
    sandbox (A03) and refuses otherwise, so no version is named.

A20 rule 3 (`02_rules_installation.md`) says the host is Linux, and its
      formal invariants gain `host = linux`. Rule 3 stays outside the running
      kernel (State 3, no owner): it is a fact of the release.

A17 rule 1 (`installation`, the configuration file and,
      through "here and in rule 2", the secret files) and A18 rule 2
      (`store`, every file of the data directory) open each component with
      `O_NOFOLLOW`, never first asking whether the flag exists; there is no
      mode without it.
judgement.why: State 6 decides that Linux is a release fact with no runtime module owner; the startup probe proves the sandbox, while installation and store use O_NOFOLLOW unconditionally.
judgement.failure: the deciding quote is not found verbatim in the later states' texts
